Task 007 stop condition (2026-08-08): Seasonal Intelligence was investigated for a possible second controlled-batch task and found NOT well-defined enough to implement without a genuine product decision. lib/marketing-memory/seasonality.ts is a 42-line recurrence classifier consumed only by Marketing Memory's own Learning-weighting pipeline (learningEvaluation.ts, rationale.ts, cohorts.ts) -- unrelated to any owner-facing forecast. The actual 'seasonal hint' shown today (lib/head-of-marketing/service.ts's seasonalCampaign, sourced from lib/marketing-planner/openai-planner.ts's OpenAI-generated Marketing Plan field) is architecturally disconnected from that classifier -- confirmed by tracing effectiveSeasonalHint (lib/marketing-director/memoryComposition.ts), which only filters the existing hint by customer content preferences, never bridges the two. docs/project-magic/SEASONAL_INTELLIGENCE.md describes six input types (previous years, competitor history, weather, search trends, campaign performance, customer behavior); real unconnected provider infrastructure already exists for several (weatherProvider.ts, trendsProvider.ts, holidayProvider.ts, localEventsProvider.ts) but nothing wires any of them into a forecast, and no doc specifies which combination constitutes a first slice, or how a real implementation should relate to the existing (and, per the doc's own design rules, non-compliant -- no confidence level, no evidence trail) AI-plan-derived hint occupying the same product surface. This was not resolved by inventing a narrower scope -- per explicit instruction, do not do that. A real Task 007 needs a product decision from Sean first: which input(s) back an MVP forecast, which surface(s) it targets, and its relationship to the existing seasonalHint.

Market Radar's monitoring/detection layer (Task 003) is scored entirely from lib/market-context/providers/competitorProvider.ts's existing profile-declared signal — there is still no live external competitor monitoring anywhere in this repository, by design; do not let a future task quietly add one without a separate, explicit scoping decision.
